newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Ringgit eases beyond 2.5120 barrier, seen falling.
newsitem.headline: Ringgit eases beyond 2.5120 barrier, seen falling.

text.p: The ringgit broke above the 2.5120 barrier against the dollar on sustained selling by overseas funds, and was expected to ease further if Bank Negara did not intervene, dealers said.
They said some U.S. investment institutions continued to build large dollar positions against the ringgit, which could pull down the Malaysian unit further in the less liquid London.
But, there was the possibility of a technical rebound between the 2.5120 and 2.5140 a dollar level, dealers said.
On Tuesday, the ringgit dipped to 2.5140 in Europe, but recovered, partly on fears of Bank Negara's intervention.
Last week, Bank Negara intervened at 2.5120 level by selling an estimated $200 million to slow down the ringgit's fall.
"Bank Negara would probably wait for the most opportune moment, when its intervention would be most effective with minimal use of its reserves," a Malaysian bank dealer said.
A U.S. bank dealer in Singapore said some U.S. funds, mostly margin players, were involved in the dollar accumulation. "The position could be a few yards (billion dollars)," he added.
At 0900 GMT, the ringgit was at 2.5125/35 a dollar.
